newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's Sime set for ninth year of record profit.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's Sime set for ninth year of record profit.

text.p: Malaysia's Sime Darby Bhd is poised to post its ninth straight year of record profits, with property and tractor divisions making up for lower overseas unit contributions, analysts said at the weekend.
The conglomerate's pre-tax profit is expected to rise to between 1.10 billion and 1.20 billion ringgit ($442-$482 million) against 1.01 billion ringgit previously, they said.
Sime's financial results for the year ended June 30, 1996 are due on Saturday.
Analysts said results from Sime's Malaysian businesses are expected to more than make up for declines in the group's Hong Kong and Singapore operations.

Sime Darby Hong Kong last Tuesday reported a net profit of HK$266.0 million, down 47.3 percent from HK$504.8 million previously. The lower profit has been expected as analysts do not expect a recovery at the Hong Kong division before 1997.
Profit from Singapore operations is also seen lower as margins on motor vehicle trading remain under severe pressure.
"Sime showed in the first half that it could make up for the lower earnings from Hong Hong and Singapore," an analyst with a British brokerage said.

Analysts said major contributors would be the property and tractor divisions while the plantations sector should also contribute positively even though crude palm oil prices in the second half-year were lower compared with the first half.
Sales of higher value products and industrial land would continue to boost earnings of the property division.

Meanwhile, the tractors division should benefit from strong sales of heavy equipment related to major infrastructure projects and stable logging activities in the East Malaysian states of Sabah and Sarawak, analysts said.
"We are maintaining our earlier forecast. Nothing unusual is expected," the British brokerage analyst said. "It will be pretty much in line with first half-year performance."
The multinational posted a pre-tax profit of 502.2 million ringgit in the first half-year, up 13 percent from the year-earlier period.
A survey of 31 stockbroking houses showed a forecast net profit of 611.3 billion ringgit for 1996, or 28.4 cents per share. Net profit in the 1994/95 financial year was 569.2 million ringgit.
Analysts, however, expect earnings to be at the lower end of the forecast range due to smaller contribution from Sime's new jewel, United Malayan Banking Corp (UMBC).
Sime's acquisition of a 60 percent stake in UMBC, Malaysia's fourth largest banking group, was completed in April this year, later than expected.
"The full impact of the acquisition will be felt from this year," said one analyst with a foreign brokerage.
He expects earnings to grow between 25 and 30 percent in the current financial year.
UBS Research (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd earlier estimated UMBC's contribution to Sime's pre-tax profit at 398.5 million ringgit in the 1996/97 financial year and 472.5 million in 1997/98.
